Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The code snippet of JarArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry(ArchiveEntry) shows that if the jarMarkerAdded flag is false, then the ArchiveEntry (cast to ZipArchiveEntry) has a JarMarker extra field added as first extra field, and then jarMarkerAdded is set to true. After that, it calls super.putArchiveEntry(ze).

This means only the very first entry added using putArchiveEntry will get the JarMarker extra field.

The test creates a JarArchiveOutputStream on a temporary file, and puts two entries: "foo/" and "bar/". The test expects the entry "foo/" to have exactly one extra field, which should be a JarMarker instance. The second entry "bar/" is expected to have zero extra fields.

The current bug report questions the public visibility and use of the finish() methods on ArchiveOutputStream implementations, saying that allowing them to be called externally may corrupt the output and only close() is necessary.

The test calls out.finish() in line 44 before calling out.close() in line 45.

The finish() method is abstract in ArchiveOutputStream but its implementation for JarArchiveOutputStream is not yet inspected. It is likely that the finish() method finalizes the archive writing, and the close() method also calls finish(), so calling finish() explicitly before close() may cause issues or may not be necessary.

The issue underlying the test failure may be related to the finish() method's behavior or to the order or presence of setting jarMarkerAdded flag in relation to finish().

I want to check the implementation of JarArchiveOutputStream.finish() and close() to understand if calling finish() explicitly is safe or if it can cause write corruption or loss of markers.

Now I will request the code snippet of JarArchiveOutputStream.finish(), as it is key to understanding this problem. Since I got multiple matches earlier, I must specify full signature for JarArchiveOutputStream.finish() if present, or else for ZipArchiveOutputStream.finish() to understand the upstream behavior.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug.
